title: Suggested Is Not Superseded: A Pre-Registered Evaluation of a System-One Model as a Memory-Retirement Gate
abstract: arXiv:2610.15710v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-term memory for assistants needs a gate that decides when a new utterance retires an old stored claim. Benchmark labels for this step mark a pair as changed or not, so they cannot tell a gate that acts on established change from one that acts on a hint. We write a task contract that separates the two (SUPERSEDED vs. NEEDS-CONFIRMATION vs. COMPATIBLE), label 500 test pairs built from STALE (change pairs plus same-user controls) with three LLM annotators and two human adjudicators (one author and a second annotator; provenance reported), and evaluate Jev, a typed "System One" decision model, under pre-registered hypotheses. Of the 179 test pairs STALE marks as changed, 72 meet the contract's bar for an established change. Jev never retired a claim on 141 same-conversation non-changes. Its failure is premature retirement: the binary gate retires 39.2% of claims whose change is only suggested. A three-way decision cuts this to 15.5% at

translated_title: 建议并非取代：一项关于“系统一”模型作为记忆退役门控的预注册评估
translated_abstract: 助手的长期记忆需要一个门控来决定何时一条新话语可以淘汰（retire）旧的已存储声明。针对这一步骤的基准标签只将文本对标记为“已变更”或“未变更”，因此无法区分针对已确定变更的门控与针对仅被提示（suggested）变更的门控。我们编写了一个任务契约来区分这两者（SUPERSEDED 已取代 vs. NEEDS-CONFIRMATION 需确认 vs. COMPATIBLE 兼容），并基于 STALE（变更对加上同用户对照组）构建了 500 个测试对，由三个 LLM 标注者和两名人工裁定者（一名作者和另一名标注者；标注来源已报告）进行标注，并在预注册假设下评估了 Jev——一个类型化的“系统一”决策模型。在 STALE 标记为已变更的 179 个测试对中，有 72 个符合契约中已确定变更的标准。Jev 在 141 个同对话内的非变更情形中从未错误地淘汰任何声明。它的失败在于过早淘汰：二元门控淘汰了 39.2% 的其变更仅被建议（尚未确定）的声明。三方决策机制将这一比例降至 15.5%……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究提出一个区分“已确定取代”、“需确认”与“兼容”的三分类任务契约，并在预注册评估中发现“系统一”模型 Jev 在非变更场景下零误淘汰，但二元门控会对仅被建议变更的声明产生 39.2% 的过早淘汰率，而三方决策可将其降至 15.5%。
en_tdlr: The study proposes a three-way task contract (SUPERSEDED vs. NEEDS-CONFIRMATION vs. COMPATIBLE) for memory retirement and, in a pre-registered evaluation, shows that the System-One model Jev makes zero false retirements on non-changes, while a binary gate prematurely retires 39.2% of merely suggested changes—a rate cut to 15.5% by the three-way decision.
